The ICD-10-CM coding manual has an Alphabetic Index and a Tabular List of Diseases and Injuries. In your own words, briefly describe the purpose and function of both the index and the tabular list as described in your assigned reading this week. Write one well-written paragraph and answer the above questions to earn 10 points.
questions_and_answers.answer: The ICD-10-CM coding manual, used for diagnosing and classifying diseases, is divided into two main sections: the Alphabetic Index and the Tabular List of Diseases and Injuries. The Alphabetic Index serves as a directory to guide users to the appropriate codes. It is organized alphabetically by disease or condition, and it includes both the disease names and synonyms, abbreviations, and cross-references. This index is the starting point for coding, as it helps users to locate the correct code. On the other hand, the Tabular List of Diseases and Injuries is a structured list of codes organized by chapters based on body system or condition. Each code in this list corresponds to a specific disease, injury, or condition. The list provides detailed information about each code, including inclusion and exclusion notes, and instructions for additional coding if necessary.
